Package cliwerk.spec

Class CommandSpecMerger

java.lang.Object
cliwerk.spec.CommandSpecMerger
public final class CommandSpecMerger extends Object
Merges one or more externally-defined CommandLine.Model.CommandSpecs (typically read from JSON with CommandSpecJson.read(String)) into a host ("uber") CommandSpec, each as a subcommand keyed by its own name.

This is the composition step for a proxy CLI: a hand-built or annotation-based uber command contributes its own top-level options/behavior, while one or more imported specs each contribute a whole subcommand namespace describing a delegated tool's CLI (e.g. flix). How a merged-in subcommand is actually executed (shelling out, an API call, etc.) is up to the uber command's own execution logic -- this class only builds the combined model.

  • Method Details

    • merge

      public static picocli.CommandLine.Model.CommandSpec merge(picocli.CommandLine.Model.CommandSpec uber, picocli.CommandLine.Model.CommandSpec... imported)
      Attaches each of the given imported specs to uber as a subcommand named after imported.name(), and returns uber. Validation via SpecValidator.validate(CommandSpec) is performed once after all imported specs are attached.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if an imported spec has no name, if uber already has a subcommand with that name, or if merging introduces one of the two parsing ambiguities SpecValidator checks for (e.g. an imported spec's name colliding with an existing option's defaultValue on uber)

    • mergeAll

      public static picocli.CommandLine.Model.CommandSpec mergeAll(picocli.CommandLine.Model.CommandSpec uber, Collection<picocli.CommandLine.Model.CommandSpec> imported)
      Attaches a collection of imported specs to uber as subcommands named after each CommandLine.Model.CommandSpec.name(), and returns uber. Validation via SpecValidator.validate(CommandSpec) is performed once after all imported specs in the collection are attached.
      Parameters:
      uber - the host command spec to receive the subcommands
      imported - the collection of command specs to attach as subcommands
      Returns:
      uber for convenience
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if an imported spec has no name, if uber already has a subcommand with that name, or if merging introduces a parsing ambiguity
